summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, recent CABG and mitral valve replacement, and chronic kidney disease was admitted from rehab for fevers and leukocytosis. Initially treated for a possible UTI, she continued to spike fevers without urinary symptoms. Workup revealed C. difficile colitis, which was treated with oral vancomycin, leading to resolution of fevers and leukocytosis. She developed acute kidney injury with rising creatinine to 3.4, likely due to infection-induced acute tubular necrosis, but recovered without dialysis. Her dialysis catheter was removed as a potential infection source, with negative tip culture. Leg swelling and pain were attributed to volume overload and diabetic neuropathy, with DVT ruled out. Insulin was optimized to prevent hypoglycemia, and warfarin was adjusted for atrial fibrillation. She improved clinically and was discharged back to rehab on a stable medication regimen with follow-up plans.
problems: Intestinal infection due to Clostridium difficile
Acute kidney failure with lesion of tubular necrosis
Type 1 diabetes mellitus, uncontrolled with complications
